To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the addition of STPP (0.4%) and NaCl (1.5%) in green mussel protein hydrolysate production by using Flavorzyme at pH of 8 and 3% (E/S) increased the umami taste.

the addition of STPP (0.4%) and NaCl (1.5%) in green mussel protein hydrolysis with flavorzyme (E/S 3%, pH 8) produced hydrolysate with highest DH (23, 18%), highest yield (8, 34%) and highest umami taste.

green mussel hydrolyzed protein produced with the presence of STPP and sodium chloride (NaCl) had higher degree of hydrolysis, darker color and highest yield, higher umami taste score and lower bitterness than those produced with enzyme only.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new food flavorant from green mussel hydrolyzed by flavorzyme with the presence of STPP and sodium chloride.
the evaluation of the umami taste of green mussel hydrolysed in the presence of STPP and/or NaCl.
the production of umami taste by using green mussel hydrolysed with flavorzyme.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the addition of STPP in the production of protein hydrolysate from green mussel resulted in a higher degree of hydrolysis, darker color and higher yield.
hydrolysates produced from green mussels in the presence of STPP and sodium chloride are more acceptable than those produced in the absence of both.
the addition of NaCl and STPP to green mussel hydrolyzate produced with flavorzyme has improved the umami taste and yield of the hydrolysate.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
hydrolysate produced using flavorzyme at enzyme substrate ratio of 3%, pH 8, in the presence of 1.5 % NaCI and 0.4 % STPP was found to be suitable for the production of umami taste.

the addition of STPP (sodium tripolyphosphate) and NaCI (sodium chloride) during enzymatic hydrolysis of green mussel (G. viridis) with flavourzyme resulted in a hydrolysate with high umaminess and low bitterness.

the hydrolysis of green mussel protein in the presence of NaCl and STPP resulted in the production of hydrolysates that are darker in color with lower molecular weight, higher yield, and higher umami taste.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the addition of sodium tripolypphosphate and NaCl in hydrolysation process can increase the umami taste of the protein hydrolysate.
the addition of STPP in combination with NaCI can improve the yield and quality of the green mussel hydrolyzed protein.
green mussel hydrolyzate produced with the addition of STPP (0.4%) and NaCI (1.5%) has a high umami score and can be used as a food flavor.
